scope: Legacy application Cloudflare parity migrations and explicit runtime grants

coverage: all seven original table snapshots and existing migration history unchanged
token ciphertext/IV/auth tag/version, sessions, VAPID bytes, subscriptions, sources and favorites retained
current generated Node client reads added fields on old rows
actual restricted runtime-role generated client reads
exact thirteen-table SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE matrix and no TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER
real notification/template identity and terminal-state guards
diagnostic sequence use and bounds; token rotation lease-pair constraint
wrong database OID rejects grants; same grant application replay succeeds
runtime migration history, schema/admin, sequence setval, ungranted future table and other-schema access denied
no explicit fixture-role grants in other databases

findings: owner blanket table defaults expose migration history unless removed
appended source grants can include the opposite environment runtime role; scoped grant script revokes it in target database

limitations: No production schema migration, restore, grant change or application cutover executed.
Local tests use the owned PostgreSQL server and synthetic fixture data; production inspection is metadata only.
Existing public CONNECT policy in unrelated databases is unchanged; the script grants no rights there.
Template job/notice retention currently has no cleanup sweep; completed identities remain stored.
